title: Modern browsers don't implement "4.10.21.2 Implicit submission" correctly
body:
I've recently discovered that modern browsers don't implement the 4.10.21.2 Implicit submission spec correctly.
This bug was reported to ... here:
- Chromium: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1305986#c4
- Bugzilla: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1759480

Tested browsers:
- Firefox 99.0b3
- Chrome 99.0.4844.51
- Edge 99.0.1150.39
- Safari 15.3
- Opera 84

_Please note that not all browsers implement all the input types and I've ignored those for my testing._

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#implicit-submission

> For the purpose of the previous paragraph, an element is a field that blocks implicit submission of a form element if it is an input element whose form owner is that form element and whose type attribute is in one of the following states:​ Text, Search, URL, Telephone, Email, Password, Date, Month, Week, Time, Local Date and Time, Number

Only the following input types are correctly implemented: text, search, url, tel, email, password, number
Meaning these input types are faulty: date, time, month, week, datetime-local

Since changing these browser's behavior would result in a compatibility issues, I'd rather update the spec (remove those 4 input types).
I myself wonder why the faulty input types are even included in this list.
